summary: Verified Google-Ads malware-flag remediation: PostHog + emergent-main.js scripts fully removed from index.html; canonical, sitemap.xml (324/324 URLs), robots.txt all point to https://www.lesjardiniersnormands.fr. Backend regression 10/10 pytest passed. Frontend: all 8 nav pages load (200), no PostHog references anywhere, contact form POST /api/contact returns 200 with email_sent=true (Resend id returned). Only one minor SEO defect found: dynamic canonical on service pages defaults to site root instead of the page-specific URL.

seo_issues.screen: /paysagiste-caen, /elagage-caen (and likely every page that does not pass a canonical prop)
seo_issues.issue: react-helmet <link rel='canonical'> resolves to 'https://www.lesjardiniersnormands.fr/' (site root) instead of the page's own URL. Root cause: SEO.jsx line 16 `const url = canonical || COMPANY.site;` — pages do not pass a `canonical` prop, so every page ends up self-canonicalising to the homepage. This causes duplicate-canonical across the whole site and will hurt SEO (though it does NOT re-trigger the Google Ads malware flag). Fix: either pass a canonical prop from each page (e.g. `${COMPANY.site}${location.pathname}`) or default to it inside SEO.jsx using useLocation().

action_items: Fix per-page canonical URLs in SEO.jsx (currently every route canonicalises to https://www.lesjardiniersnormands.fr/). Use useLocation() or pass canonical prop from each page.
critical_code_review_comments: public/index.html is now clean (no PostHog, no emergent-main.js) — malware pattern removed at source.
sitemap.xml: 324/324 <loc> on production domain, zero references to emergent.host / preview URL.
SEO.jsx default canonical falls back to COMPANY.site (root) — this is a real SEO defect for all inner pages. Recommended to derive canonical from React Router useLocation.
